question.problem:
The function $g(x)$ is continuous over $x\in [-1,2].$ Some values of $g(x)$ are given in the table below. 

| $x$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $g(x)$ | $2$ | $0$ | $3$ |

What is the smallest possible number of solutions to the equation $g(x)=1?$
question.worked_solution:
Since $g$ is a continuous function on $[-1,2]$, we can apply the intermediate value theorem (IVT) in any subinterval of $[-1,2].$

We will go through each subinterval of $[-1,2]$ and check if the IVT guarantees a solution to the equation $g(x)=1$ on this interval.

- On the subinterval $[-1,1],$ we have $g(-1)=2$ and $g(1)=0.$ Since $1\in [0,2],$ the IVT *does* guarantee a solution to the equation $g(x)=1$ on this subinterval.

- On the subinterval $[1,2],$ we have $g(1)=0$ and $g(2)=3.$ Since $1\in [0,3],$ the IVT  *does* guarantee a solution to the equation $g(x)=1$ on this subinterval.

The IVT guarantees solutions to $g(x)=1$ on the subintervals $[-1,1]$ and $[1,2].$ Therefore, $g(x)=1$ has at least two solutions.
